tier_reasons.primary: Complete retained cohorts with valid matched splits and adequate cross-cohort comparability.
tier_reasons.stress_test: Valid splits retained as scientifically useful boundary cases, but treatment, lesion, or strongly different task structure limits direct comparability.
tier_reasons.descriptive_only: Valid split, but the released sample is too small for cross-cohort inference.
tier_reasons.quarantined: The frozen result violates the intended within-condition transfer estimand and is excluded from every correlation, ranking, and direction count.

kwak.reason: The current manifest adapts on CNO sessions and tests on DMSO sessions, confounding subject adaptation with treatment transfer.
kwak.split_contract: Retain DMSO/control sessions only for every subject; adapt on chronological odd-indexed DMSO sessions and test on chronological even-indexed DMSO sessions. Never adapt on one treatment and score another treatment.

categorical_distance.description: Outcome-blind task-design annotations extracted from the cited Methods sections.
categorical_distance.distance_rule: Equal-weight Gower/Hamming mismatch, minimized over the three source-task prototypes. A list-valued annotation matches when either task value overlaps the prototype value. No weights or annotations use GRU results.

contract.schedule_summary: Compute within-session metrics per subject, then average subjects equally within each cohort.
contract.empirical_schedule_distance: Root-mean-square standardized Euclidean distance to Grossman across the declared distance features; standardization uses only the six primary, non-quarantined complete-probability cohorts.
contract.inference: Primary Spearman inference uses eight primary cohorts for categorical distance and six primary complete-probability cohorts for schedule distance. The all-valid categorical sensitivity uses 12 non-quarantined cohorts. Exact two-sided permutation is used for n<=8; otherwise deterministic 100,000-draw permutation; all analyses use 20,000 cohort bootstraps and a leave-one-cohort-out range.
